name: Bandol

limits: For red wine, Carignan and Syrah, each: at most 10%
For rosé wine, Bourboulenc, Carignan, Clairette, Syrah and Ugni Blanc, each: at most 10%
For rosé wine, Bourboulenc, Carignan, Clairette, Syrah and Ugni Blanc together: at most 20%
For white wine, Marsanne, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, each: at most 10%
For white wine, Vermentino: at most 20%
For white wine, Marsanne, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Vermentino together: at most 20%

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

notes: Red Bandol is dark, with rich flavors of black fruit, vanilla, cinnamon and leather.
It usually needs at least 10 years to fully develop, though some is made to drink after three.
Bandol rosé is spicy and earthy, sometimes with strawberry notes.

blurb.text: A Provence appellation around Bandol, Le Castellet and Sanary-sur-Mer for red, rosé and white wine. Reds must be 50 to 95 percent Mourvèdre, with Grenache and Cinsault as the other main grapes. Whites are based on Clairette, Bourboulenc and Ugni Blanc.
